task: Write one sentence of your own using the word withhold. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know withhold should be able to work it out from your sentence.

Delay is milder than withhold: a delayed payment is merely late and still on its way, while a withheld one is being deliberately kept back until the holder chooses to release it.
Deny is stronger than withhold: withholding keeps the thing back for now, with the door still ajar, while denying shuts it — the request is refused outright.

Withhold means to hold back something that is yours to give — payment, permission, information — and decline, for now, to hand it over.
The inspector withheld her signature on the elevator permit — one bolt grade didn't match the drawings — and the building sat finished but unopenable until the contractor produced the paperwork.
Withholding is refusal with a hand still on the door: the signature exists, the inspector may yet give it, and everyone knows what would release it.
That expectation is the word's engine — you can only withhold what someone is waiting to receive.
Withhold wants three things in the frame: a holder, a thing that is theirs to give, and someone waiting for it.
Taxes are withheld from paychecks, consent is withheld, names are withheld from reports.
It is not a verb of muscle — guards restrain a crowd, walls withstand storms — and it is not mere possession: a museum keeps its meteorite; nobody says it withholds it unless someone is asking.

The community center's new wing is nearly done, but the builder and the bank are locked in a quiet standoff.
Citing a leaky roof seam, the bank has chosen to withhold the final payment -- the money is approved, set aside, and sitting in an account.
The builder calls the sum his by right and points at the finished walls; the bank agrees he will get it, just not yet.
Nothing about the standoff is hidden: both sides state their positions in polite letters, copied to the center's board.
The day the seam passes inspection, the transfer goes through -- which is exactly what makes the holdback a lever rather than a punishment.
